nameEn: Bachelor of Science in Speech and Hearing Sciences

bullets: Minimum DSE requirements: 4 core subjects + 2 electives with Level 3 in English and Chinese, Level 2 in Maths and Liberal Studies; Biology or Physics preferred for audiology pathway
Typical admission score: median 28 points (Best 6 subjects), lower quartile ~26, upper quartile ~30 — competitive due to professional registration pathway
Preferred electives: Biology (for anatomy and physiology), English (for language analysis), Psychology, or Linguistics; strong communication skills essential

Interview: Required for shortlisted candidates — assesses communication clarity, empathy, understanding of speech therapy profession, and motivation for helping individuals with communication disorders
Alternative entry: IB (28+ points), GCE A-Level (ABB), relevant healthcare or education diplomas with outstanding performance, mature applicant scheme for experienced teaching assistants

Year 1: Foundation sciences — Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Hearing, Phonetics and Phonology, Introduction to Linguistics, Developmental Psychology; 40 hours observation at speech therapy clinics

Year 2: Core speech and hearing sciences — Speech Science, Hearing Science, Language Development and Disorders, Articulation and Phonological Disorders; 150 hours supervised clinical practicum (diagnostic observation)

Year 3: Clinical practice — Aural Rehabilitation, Fluency Disorders, Voice Disorders, Neurogenic Communication Disorders; 300 hours direct clinical practicum with clients under supervision at HKU Speech, Language and Hearing Clinic

Year 4: Advanced clinical and research — Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC), Swallowing Disorders, Clinical Research Methods; 400 hours advanced clinical practicum; honours research project or case study portfolio; preparation for IASH registration examination

Clinical facilities: HKU Speech, Language and Hearing Clinic — on-campus clinic serving 1,000+ clients annually; audiology suite with sound-treated booths, audiometers, and hearing aid fitting equipment; speech science lab with acoustic analysis software (Praat, WaveSurfer)

Accreditation: Programme fully accredited by the Hong Kong Institute of Speech Therapists (HKIST); graduates eligible for registration as speech therapists (ST) with the Supplementary Medical Professions Council (SMPC)
Interdisciplinary options: Minor in Psychology, Special Education, or Gerontology; joint clinical placements with HKU Faculty of Medicine and Queen Mary Hospital

Speech Therapy: Registered speech therapist at HA hospitals (Queen Mary, Prince of Wales), special schools, private clinics, or early education centres; starting salaries HK$30,000-40,000/month after SMPC registration

Audiology: Clinical audiologist at HA hospitals, hearing aid centres, or cochlear implant programmes; requires additional Master's in Audiology for full registration; starting salaries HK$28,000-38,000/month
Education: Special education teacher with speech therapy focus; learning support coordinator at mainstream schools; educational consultant for language development programmes

Research & Academia: PhD in Communication Sciences and Disorders; research positions at universities or teaching hospitals; focus on bilingual language acquisition, autism spectrum disorders, or voice science
Private Practice: Independent speech therapy clinic owner; multidisciplinary practice with occupational therapists and psychologists; average private session fees HK$800-1,500/hour
Further Studies: Master's in Speech Therapy (overseas: UCL, University of Sydney, Northwestern University), Audiology, or Special Education; professional doctorate (SLPD) for clinical leadership

Clinical facilities: HKU Speech, Language and Hearing Clinic at Meng Wah Complex — 8 therapy rooms, 2 sound-treated audiology booths, parent observation rooms, and resource library; serves paediatric and adult clients with communication and swallowing disorders
Speech science lab: Acoustic analysis workstations (Praat, WaveSurfer), electropalatography system, nasometry equipment, laryngoscopy suite; supports research in voice science and articulation

Audiology suite: Diagnostic audiometers, tympanometers, otoacoustic emission analysers, hearing aid programming software (NOAH), real-ear measurement systems; supports hearing assessment and rehabilitation training

Libraries: Main Library speech and hearing sciences collection; online access to Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders; dedicated subject librarian

Student societies: Speech and Hearing Sciences Society organises case study discussions, clinical skills workshops, volunteer visits to special schools, and advocacy events for communication accessibility
Admission statistics: ~600 applicants for ~100 places (6:1 ratio) — highly competitive due to guaranteed professional registration and strong employment prospects
Score distribution: 70% of admitted students score 26-30 points; students with 24-25 need exceptional communication skills or relevant healthcare volunteering experience
Communication skills premium: Strong English and Chinese (Cantonese) proficiency essential; interview heavily weights clarity of expression, empathy, and understanding of speech therapy role

Comparison with PolyU Speech Therapy (JS3638): HKU has stronger research focus and medical school links; PolyU has larger intake (~150 places) and more practice-oriented curriculum with earlier clinical exposure

Non-JUPAS intake: ~15% of places for international students and mature applicants with healthcare or education backgrounds; Mandarin proficiency increasingly valued for serving mainland Chinese clients
Trend: Growing demand for speech therapists due to ageing population and increased autism awareness; government expanding speech therapy services in schools and elderly care; 2024 applications up 20%
Dr. Catherine Lam (BSc 1985) — Chief Speech Therapist at Hospital Authority, overseeing speech therapy services across 43 public hospitals and 70+ special schools
Ms. Anita Wong (BSc 1992) — Founder of Speech Therapy Associates, largest private speech therapy group in Hong Kong with 15 clinics and 50+ therapists
Dr. Raymond Lee (BSc 1998, PhD 2004) — Professor of Speech and Hearing Sciences at HKU, leading researcher in bilingual language development and Cantonese phonology
Ms. Emily Chan (BSc 2005) — Head of Audiology at Queen Mary Hospital, managing cochlear implant programme and newborn hearing screening for Hong Kong
Mr. Kevin So (BSc 2010) — Director of Rehabilitation at SAHK (Society for the Relief of Disabled), leading community-based speech therapy for adults with intellectual disabilities
HKU Foundation Entrance Scholarship: Full tuition + HK$50,000/year for DSE 5** in 3+ subjects; speech and hearing sciences students with strong academic and communication skills frequently qualify
Faculty of Education Scholarship: HK$25,000-35,000/year for top 10% of cohort based on academic and clinical performance
Hospital Authority Speech Therapy Scholarship: Full tuition + HK$10,000/month during clinical years; requires 3-year HA service as registered speech therapist after graduation
Hearing Aid Industry Scholarship: HK$30,000/year for students specialising in audiology; includes internship at major hearing aid manufacturers (Phonak, Oticon, Widex)
Overseas Clinical Placement Grant: HK$35,000 for elective clinical placement at overseas speech therapy centres (Australia, UK, Canada); covers travel and accommodation
Develop strong bilingual skills: Fluency in both English and Cantonese is essential; many clients are bilingual children or elderly Cantonese speakers; Mandarin is an additional advantage

Gain exposure to special needs: Volunteer at special schools, autism support centres, or elderly care homes; interviewers value candidates who understand the realities of working with communication disorders
Shadow a speech therapist: Arrange observation at HA hospitals or private clinics; understanding the day-to-day work (assessments, therapy sessions, parent consultations) strengthens your application
Prepare for the interview: Practice explaining complex concepts simply, demonstrate empathy through role-play scenarios, and research current issues (bilingualism, teletherapy, AAC technology)

Consider the emotional demands: Speech therapy requires patience, resilience, and emotional intelligence; ensure you are prepared for working with clients who may have lifelong communication challenges
最低文憑試要求：4科核心科目 + 2科選修科目，英文及中文達3級，數學及通識達2級；優先考慮生物或物理（聽覺學途徑）
典型入學分數：中位數28分（最佳6科），下四分位數約26分，上四分位數約30分——因專業註冊途徑而具競爭性
優先選修科目：生物（解剖及生理學）、英文（語言分析）、心理學或語言學；強勁溝通技巧至關重要
面試：入圍候選人必須面試——評估溝通清晰度、同理心、對言語治療專業的理解及幫助溝通障礙人士的熱誠
替代入學途徑：IB（28分以上）、GCE A-Level（ABB）、相關醫療或教育文憑並有卓越表現、有經驗教學助理成熟申請人計劃
第一年：基礎科學——言語及聽覺解剖生理學、語音學及音系學、語言學導論、發展心理學；40小時言語治療診所觀察
第二年：核心言語及聽覺科學——言語科學、聽覺科學、語言發展與障礙、構音及音系障礙；150小時監督臨床實習（診斷觀察）
第三年：臨床實踐——聽覺康復、流暢障礙、嗓音障礙、神經性溝通障礙；於港大言語、語言及聽覺診所進行300小時直接臨床實習（監督下接見個案）
第四年：高級臨床及研究——輔助及替代溝通（AAC）、吞嚥障礙、臨床研究方法；400小時高級臨床實習；榮譽研究項目或個案研究組合；預備IASH註冊考試
臨床設施：港大言語、語言及聽覺診所——每年服務1,000多名個案的校內診所；聽覺學套房設有隔音室、聽力計及助聽器調配設備；言語科學實驗室配備聲學分析軟件（Praat、WaveSurfer）
認證：課程獲香港言語治療師公會（HKIST）全面認可；畢業生符合向輔助醫療業管理局（SMPC）註冊為言語治療師（ST）資格
跨學科選項：心理學、特殊教育或老年學副修；與港大醫學院及瑪麗醫院聯合臨床實習
言語治療：於醫管局醫院（瑪麗醫院、威爾斯親王醫院）、特殊學校、私人診所或早期教育中心擔任註冊言語治療師；SMPC註冊後起薪每月30,000-40,000港元
聽覺學：於醫管局醫院、助聽器中心或人工耳蝸計劃擔任臨床聽覺學家；需額外修讀聽覺學碩士方可全面註冊；起薪每月28,000-38,000港元
教育界：具言語治療專長的特殊教育教師；主流學校學習支援統籌員；語言發展計劃教育顧問
研究及學術界：溝通科學與障礙博士；大學或教學醫院研究職位；專注雙語語言習得、自閉症譜系障礙或嗓音科學
私人執業：獨立言語治療診所東主；與職業治療師及心理學家組成跨專業實踐；平均私人診症費每小時800-1,500港元
進修：海外言語治療碩士（倫敦大學學院、悉尼大學、西北大學）、聽覺學或特殊教育碩士；臨床領導專業博士（SLPD）
臨床設施：蒙民偉樓港大言語、語言及聽覺診所——8間治療室、2間隔音聽覺學室、家長觀察室及資源圖書館；為有溝通及吞嚥障礙的兒童及成人提供服務
言語科學實驗室：聲學分析工作站（Praat、WaveSurfer）、電子顎圖系統、鼻流量儀器、喉鏡套房；支援嗓音科學及構音研究
聽覺學套房：診斷聽力計、鼓室圖儀、耳聲發射分析儀、助聽器編程軟件（NOAH）、真耳測量系統；支援聽力評估及康復訓練
圖書館：主圖書館言語及聽覺科學藏書；可線上使用Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research、International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders；專責學科圖書館員
學生學會：言語及聽覺科學學會組織個案研討、臨床技能工作坊、特殊學校義工探訪及溝通無障礙倡議活動
入學統計：約600人申請，約100個學額（6:1比例）——因保證專業註冊及強勁就業前景而競爭激烈
分數分佈：70%獲錄取學生達26-30分；24-25分者需有卓越溝通技巧或相關醫療義工經驗
溝通技巧溢價：精通英文及中文（粵語）至關重要；面試高度重視表達清晰度、同理心及對言語治療角色的理解
與理大言語治療（JS3638）比較：港大研究重點較強及醫學院聯繫較佳；理大收生較多（約150學額）及較早臨床接觸的實踐導向課程
非聯招收生：約15%學額予國際學生及有醫療或教育背景的成熟申請人；普通話能力對服務內地客戶日益受重視
趨勢：因人口老化及自閉症意識提升，言語治療師需求日增；政府擴展學校及長者護理言語治療服務；2024年申請增加20%
林嘉儀博士（1985年言語及聽覺科學學士）——醫管局首席言語治療師，管理43間公營醫院及70多間特殊學校言語治療服務
黃雅文女士（1992年言語及聽覺科學學士）——Speech Therapy Associates創辦人，香港最大私人言語治療集團，擁有15間診所及50多名治療師
李偉強博士（1998年言語及聽覺科學學士，2004年博士）——港大言語及聽覺科學教授，雙語語言發展及粵語音系學領先研究者
陳詠琪女士（2005年言語及聽覺科學學士）——瑪麗醫院聽覺學主管，管理人工耳蝸計劃及香港新生兒聽力篩查
蘇家豪先生（2010年言語及聽覺科學學士）——香港弱能人士護助會康復總監，領導智障成人社區言語治療
港大基金入學獎學金：全額學費 + 每年50,000港元（文憑試3科以上5**）；學術及溝通技巧強的言語及聽覺科學學生經常符合資格
教育學院獎學金：每年25,000-35,000港元予前10%學生，按學術及臨床表現評選
醫管局言語治療獎學金：全額學費 + 臨床年份每月10,000港元；畢業後需於醫管局擔任註冊言語治療師3年
助聽器業界獎學金：每年30,000港元予專修聽覺學學生；包括主要助聽器製造商（Phonak、Oticon、Widex）實習
海外臨床實習資助：35,000港元供海外言語治療中心（澳洲、英國、加拿大）選修臨床實習；涵蓋旅費及住宿
發展強勁雙語能力：精通英文及粵語至關重要；許多個案為雙語兒童或粵語長者；普通話為額外優勢
接觸特殊需要：於特殊學校、自閉症支援中心或長者護理院當義工；面試官重視了解與溝通障礙人士工作現實的候選人
跟隨言語治療師：安排於醫管局醫院或私人診所觀察；了解日常工作（評估、治療環節、家長諮詢）強化申請
準備面試：練習簡單解釋複雜概念、透過角色扮演展示同理心、研究時事議題（雙語主義、遙距治療、AAC科技）
考慮情感需求：言語治療需要耐心、抗逆力及情緒智商；確保你準備好與可能有終身溝通挑戰的個案工作
